privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.short: This site has no account, no database and no tracking. It asks for nothing about you.
privacy.storage: Your favourites, your board (the software you ticked) and your Windows / Mac choice are kept in your browser, on your device. They never go to a server, do not travel between devices, and disappear if you clear the browser's data.
privacy.cookies: None. What the site keeps is needed to make it work as you asked, so no consent banner is required.
privacy.logs: Vercel, the host, records technical logs of each visit, which contain IP addresses, to run and protect the service (legitimate interest). These logs may be processed in the United States, under the safeguards Vercel provides (Data Privacy Framework and standard contractual clauses), and are kept for a limited time set by the host. Klacki neither reads nor uses them.
privacy.rights: As nothing about you is kept on a Klacki server, there is nothing to access, correct or delete on its side. To erase what your browser keeps, clear the site's data. For the host's logs, contact Vercel. You may also lodge a complaint with your data protection authority (in France, the CNIL: cnil.fr).
privacy.controller: Lucas Nevano, publisher of the site (see the legal notice).

sources.title: Sources
sources.intro: Every shortcut is checked against the publisher's own documentation. Here is the page used for each software, with the version and the date it was checked.

about.title: About
about.what: One place for the keyboard shortcuts of creative software: 3D, texturing, VFX, video and 2D. The promise is simple: find a shortcut in under five seconds.
about.how: Shortcuts live in one file per software, checked when the site is built: a wrong or incomplete file stops the build instead of reaching you. Pages are generated ahead of time, so the site stays fast.
about.who: Lucas Nevano, a junior full-stack developer in France. Klacki is a portfolio project.
about.correction: Shortcuts change from one version to the next. If one is wrong, tell me and it gets fixed.

home.lede: Your software, their Windows and Mac keys, read one by one in the publisher's own documentation. The list keeps growing.

tour.title: What Klacki does for you
tour.lede: Six things, in the order you will need them.

search.title: Search an action or a key
search.text: Type "undo", "extrude" or "F9": every software answers at once, accents and word order ignored.

platform.title: Windows or Mac, in one click
platform.text: The switch in the header rewrites every key. And the site tells you when Ctrl does not become ⌘: the rows here come straight from the data.
platform.cta: What changes between Windows and Mac

keyboard.title: See where the keys are
keyboard.text: Hover the keys of a shortcut, or tap them on a phone: a keyboard appears with the right keys lit, plus the numeric pad and the mouse when needed.

board.title: Put your software side by side
board.text: You know Maya and you are learning Blender? Tick both: each action becomes a card, and the traps are flagged, when the same keys do something else elsewhere. Share your board with a link.

keep.title: Keep what you use
keep.text: The star puts a shortcut in your favourites, the button next to it copies the whole line for your notes. Everything stays in your browser: no account to create.

trust.title: Never guessed
trust.text: Every shortcut comes from the publisher's official documentation, with the version and the date it was checked. When it says nothing, the page says so instead of making it up.

catalogue.title: The software covered
catalogue.lede: One software, one page: its shortcuts sorted by category, its version, and the link to the documentation used as the reference.
catalogue.missingText: Say so, with a link to its official documentation. That is how the list grows.

platforms.title: Windows or Mac, without the traps
platforms.lede: Many lists swap Ctrl for ⌘ automatically. That is wrong half of the time: Blender, Maya and Houdini keep Ctrl on Mac. Here every Mac key is read in the documentation, one by one. Use the toggle above and watch.
platforms.demoTitle: Real shortcuts, taken from the data of this site

rules.title: Ctrl does not always become ⌘
rules.text: Blender, Maya and Houdini keep Ctrl on Mac. Adobe and Foundry software switch to ⌘.

rules.title: Alt is called Option
rules.text: Same physical key, another name. The site shows ⌥ without pretending the shortcut changed.

rules.title: And when the software has no Mac version?
rules.text: Some software is Windows only. Its page says so, and the toggle does not invent a Mac key.

platforms.memo: Your Windows or Mac choice is kept in your browser: you make it once, the site remembers.
platforms.layoutTitle: And if your keyboard is not a US QWERTY?
platforms.layoutLede: Publishers write their documentation for an American keyboard, in QWERTY. That is what the site shows, as it stands. On a French AZERTY, some letters sit elsewhere.

layoutSwaps.text: The select-all of a good many applications.
The undo key, the most worn of all.
Digits need Shift, except on the numeric pad.

platforms.layoutWarning: And it depends on the application. Some follow the letter: you press the key marked Z on your AZERTY and it undoes. Others follow the physical position, so you have to press W. Publishers rarely say which. Klacki shows the key as it is documented and stops there — guessing the rest would be lying.
platforms.layoutOther: On a German QWERTZ, Y and Z trade places.

notFound.title: This page does not exist
notFound.text: The address is wrong, or the page moved. The catalogue and the search are two steps away.

board.title: My board
board.lede: Pick the software you know and the ones you are learning. For each action the keys are grouped with the software that use them, and the ones that would betray your old reflexes are marked.
board.invite: Pick at least two software to compare them.
board.none: These software have no action in common yet.
board.share: Copy the link to this board
board.sharedTitle: A board someone shared with you

sections.title: Purpose
sections.text: Klacki gathers the keyboard shortcuts of creative software. These terms govern the use of klacki.vercel.app. Using the site means accepting them.

sections.title: Access
sections.text: The site is free, with no sign-up and no account. It is provided as is: it may be interrupted, changed or stopped at any time, without notice.

sections.title: Accuracy of the shortcuts
sections.text: Every shortcut is taken from the publisher's official documentation, whose version and check date are shown. A publisher may change its shortcuts, and your own setup may differ: check in the software before relying on one. Report a mistake with the "Suggest a correction" link.

sections.title: Intellectual property
sections.text: Software names and trademarks belong to their publishers; Klacki is not affiliated with them. Key combinations are facts. The texts, design, ghost illustrations and code of the site belong to its publisher: reproducing them requires permission.

sections.title: Data in your browser
sections.text: Your favourites, your board and your Windows / Mac choice stay in your browser. You can erase them at any time by clearing the site's data. The details are on the Privacy page.

sections.title: Liability
sections.text: The publisher cannot be held liable for any damage arising from the use of the site or from a shortcut that does not work as described. Links to publishers' documentation lead to sites it does not control.

sections.title: Changes and governing law
sections.text: These terms may change; the online version prevails. They are governed by French law.
